title: Practice 4: Short adjectives: занят, готов, рад

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Чтение ___ (эквивалентный) мышлению при помощи чужой головы, а не своей собственной.
exercises.prompt: Reading is equivalent to thinking with someone else's head instead of with one's own.
exercises.why: Many Russian adjectives have two forms, the long form and the short form: здоровый — здоров; молодой — молод; свободный — свободен. By far the most common is the long form which can be used either as a modifier or as a predicate: *Это новый автомобиль. Этот автомобиль новый.* There is, however, a limited number of adjectives that normally take the short form when used predicatively: *Это больной человек.* but *Этот человек болен.* The past and future are formed by the use of the verb "быть": *Вчера я был занят. Завтра я буду свободен.* The short form of an adjective can never be used as a modifier. — From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 57.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Many Russian adjectives have two forms, the long form and the short form: здоровый — здоров; молодой — молод; свободный — свободен. (From the DLI Grammar Reference Book, Lesson 57)
